title: What's New: Customer-Managed Encryption Key & Lockbox (2024 release wave 2)

chapters.title: Linking Business Central to Power Platform

features.name: Customer-Managed Encryption Key
features.description: A setting that allows administrators to encrypt Business Central and Power Platform environment databases with their own key managed in their own key vault rather than a Microsoft-managed key.
caveats: Requires linked Power Platform managed environment
Requires specific licensing in Microsoft 365 and Power Platform
Some downtime occurs during encryption key re-encryption
Must remain linked to maintain encryption with customer key
Copy and restore operations create new environments with Microsoft-managed encryption

features.name: Lockbox Settings
features.description: Settings administered in the Power Platform admin center that help secure environments for advanced security and privacy needs.
caveats: Administered in Power Platform admin center
Requires linked Business Central environment to Power Platform environment

features.name: Environment Linking
features.description: The ability to link a Business Central environment to a Power Platform environment in the same region and type through the Business Central admin center.
caveats: Environments must be in the same region
Environments must be of the same type (production)
Inherited settings include customer-managed encryption key and lockbox

features.name: Enterprise Policy Resource
features.description: A resource in Azure that acts as the bridge between the encryption key and environment databases, enabling the key to be used for encryption.
caveats: Must be in the same region as Power Platform and Business Central environments
Requires Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User role assignment
Requires environment administrator with ENT role to apply
